Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Claremont Primary School and thank you for visiting our website. We hope that it will provide you with useful information about our school and will introduce you to our educational and personal values.
I strongly believe in our Equality Statement that at Claremont we believe and recognise that the diversity of our community is one of our greatest strengths and assets. We are committed to ensuring that our pupils are treated fairly, and we have carefully considered and analysed the impact of our policies and procedures to promote equality of opportunity for all. We will use our position of influence as a school to work with all stakeholders to eliminate discriminatory barriers and ensure that our pupils have a sense of shared, common belonging and understanding

There are a number of clubs and activities at Claremont. Some are run by staff and others by organisations independent from the school. Please see below for the list.
For clubs that are run by outside organisations, please contact them directly. All arrangements are made through them and are independent of the school office. Fees apply to external clubs.

Welcome from the Chair of Governors
At Claremont, the Governing Body works closely with the Headteacher and Senior Leadership Team to ensure all pupils achieve their full potential, enjoy their school experience, and are kept safe.
Our governors are volunteers who bring a wide range of skills, experience and professional expertise across the operational areas of the school, helping to support effective strategic leadership.
We work collaboratively as a team, supporting our staff in a positive and constructive manner while valuing their professionalism, expertise, commitment and dedication. Claremont is fortunate to have an exceptional staff team who go above and beyond every day to help pupils achieve academically, socially and emotionally within a calm, happy and safe environment.
Governors visit the school regularly as part of our monitoring role. We have link governors for key curriculum areas, as well as designated leads for Curriculum, Safeguarding, SEND, Health and Safety, Allergy Awareness, Personnel and Finance. Through our committee meetings and Full Governing Body meetings, we review school performance, monitor progress, oversee policies and resources, and consider how we can continue to improve outcomes for all children. We also act as a critical friend, providing both support and challenge while promoting the school's vision and values.
As governors, we have strategic responsibility for the school's direction and hold the Headteacher to account for educational performance, pupil outcomes and staff performance management. We oversee the school's finances, ensuring the long-term financial viability of the school. This supports school development, the effective use of resources and the delivery of the greatest benefit to our pupils.
As Chair of Governors, I am immensely proud of Claremont and of our dedicated staff and governors. With the continued support of our parents and wider school community, I look forward to working together to ensure every child enjoys a rewarding learning journey and thrives in a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment.
With best wishes for a happy and successful time at Claremont.
Janice Logan Chair of Governors

Intent
Claremont aims to provide a high-quality mathematics education that provides a foundation for understanding the world, the ability to reason mathematically, an appreciation of the beauty and power of mathematics, and a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject. There is a balance of fluency, problem solving and reasoning following KCC guidance of progression. The children make use of manipulatives (equipment), working walls, the outdoors and each other in order to develop their understanding. Teachers develop children's independent higher order thinking skills. When children are able to describe, represent, explain, and create their own example of a concept, idea or technique, they are demonstrating 'mastery'. When children are able to solve problems of greater complexity, demonstrating creativity and imagination, independently explore and investigate, communicate results clearly, and systematically explain and generalise, they are working at greater depth.
